title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Server Room — the datacenter of your own portfolio. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Server Room
options.lineage: the datacenter rack in a hot climate: brushed panels, cable lacing, silkscreen labels, status LEDs
options.thesis: The portfolio becomes the server room of its own author: every section is a rack panel, every project a blinking status LED.
options.viewport: A rack of panels fills the hero: the FB monogram as a lit server badge, the role as a silkscreen label, and a live row of project status LEDs — real facts, each light mapped to a real project.
options.risk: Gadget-y if the LEDs never mean anything — every light must map to a real project or metric.
options.case: Assigned by the roll. Fuses cleanly: DevOps is his real production work (2-VPS AURA architecture, CI/CD Miss ESGIS, Docker everywhere).

options.label: Neon Circuit
options.lineage: hand-bent neon signage: one continuous glass tube, electrodes, gas discharge
options.thesis: The FB monogram as a single bent glass tube; the page is the circuit that keeps it lit.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for the monogram hero, loses on audience identification: neon is global signage, not the francophone-African tech scene the recruiters live in.
options.viewport: One continuous cobalt 'FB' stroke drawn across a dark room; the nav and sections are the transformer circuit feeding it.
options.risk: Typographic legibility at small sizes; novelty can age fast.

options.label: Drum Machine
options.lineage: early-80s rhythm machine step row: sixteen candy keys under a chase light
options.thesis: Career and projects as a sixteen-step row with a chase light: 'now' is always lit.
options.case: Strong interaction — steps are projects, the chase light is the timeline — but music gear reads western, not his scene.
options.viewport: A full-width step row under the hero: each step is a project, tapping it lights and opens it; the chase light sweeps with your scroll.
options.risk: Sixteen steps can trivialize a long career; key metaphor needs a legend.

options.label: Torn Flyer Wall
options.lineage: club wall of stapled flyers, torn back in strips to expose earlier nights
options.thesis: The project gallery as a wall of flyers: tear a strip back to reveal the earlier work underneath.
options.case: Best fit for 'show everything' — layers solve browsing dozens of projects — but club-culture, not tech; needs strict scanability.
options.viewport: A bright wall of flyer-like project cards; pulling a tear strip exposes the project generation beneath it.
options.risk: Dense and busy by nature — readability must be engineered hard.

canonCard.label: Category Standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark developer-portfolio grid this category always ships — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Hero, project cards, socials — the arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
